# Monavi Collection — Social Media Automation

Creates on-brand posts, stories and reels for **Monavi Collection** (family fashion boutique, India). Content is reviewed in a **PR**; **merging to main** runs a GitHub Action that schedules everything in **Buffer** (Instagram + Facebook). WhatsApp files are prepared for manual sharing because Buffer has no WhatsApp support. See README.md for the full guide and `brand/FASHION_EDITORIAL_PLAYBOOK.md` for editorial art direction and prompt engineering rules.

## Layout

- `brand/`: brand source of truth. `brand.json` (tokens + **product catalogue**), `tokens.css`, `README.md`, `voice.md`, `fonts/`, `logo/`, `elements/`, `mockups/`, `reference-posts/`, `FASHION_EDITORIAL_PLAYBOOK.md`
- `content/posts|reels/<slug>.json`: creative briefs · `content/schedule/<slug>.json`: Buffer schedule plans (immutable after merge)
- `assets/photos/<slug>/`: imported product photos · `assets/audio/`: licensed music
- `scripts/`: TypeScript run directly by Node ≥ 22.18 (type stripping, no build step)
  - `import-photo.ts`, `draw-product.ts` (vector illustration), `fashion-image.ts` (photorealistic AI fashion campaign generation & product preservation), `render-post.ts`, `render-reel.ts`, `check-media.ts`, `publish-plan.ts`, `buffer.ts`, `doctor.ts` (readiness), `clean-output.ts` + `clean-content.ts` + `clean-merged.ts` + `clean-branches.ts` (safe cleanup)
  - `lib/` (brand, quality, output, ffmpeg, buffer-api, fashion-intelligence, fashion-image-engine, reel-storyboard, social-content, media-url) · `templates/` (post.ts: overlay/arch/split/card/banner · reel.ts · illustration.ts)
- `output/<platform>/<slug>/`: delivery files + caption.txt (**committed** in content PRs) · `output/_masters/<slug>/`: manifests (committed), 2× PNG masters (ignored)
- `.github/workflows/`: `content-check.yml` (PR validation + dry run) · `schedule-on-merge.yml` (Buffer scheduling)
- `.agents/skills/`: **user commands** `setup-social-automation` · `plan-social-content` · `create-social-content` (main) · `create-social-poster` · `create-social-banner` · `edit-social-content` · `check-social-status` · `clean-social-output` · `publish-social-now` · `indian-fashion-intelligence` · `fashion-image-engine` · `fashion-reel-storyboard` · `fashion-copywriting`. **Internal steps** (hidden from `/`): `monavi-brand-rules`, `render-social-post`, `render-social-reel`, `write-social-captions`, `open-content-pr`. Use cases for each: `docs/SKILLS.md`
- `AGENTS.md` + `.agents/skills|agents/`: **generated** copies of `CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/skills/` and `.agents/agents/` for Google Antigravity (it does not read `.claude/`). Never edit them by hand
- `.agents/agents/`: `fashion-creative-director` · `fashion-product-intelligence` · `fashion-image-generator` · `brand-design-typography` · `social-media-strategist` · `reel-video-creative` · `creative-quality-assurance` · `monavi-content-strategist` · `caption-writer` · `monavi-brand-guardian`

## Commands

```bash
npm run import:photo -- "<photo>" --slug <slug> [--ai-generated]
npm run draw:product -- --slug <slug> --product <sherwani|kurta-pajama> [--occasion wedding|festive|everyday]
npm run fashion:image -- --slug <slug> --query "<prompt>" [--input-photo <photo>]
npm run render:post -- content/posts/<slug>.json [--formats ig-feed,story,pin]
npm run render:reel -- content/reels/<slug>.json [--draft]
npm run check:media -- output/instagram/<slug>
npm run plan -- validate content/schedule/<slug>.json
npm run plan -- run --files content/schedule/<slug>.json --dry-run
npm run sync:antigravity -- [--check]            # regenerate AGENTS.md and .agents/ from CLAUDE.md and .claude/ (CI runs --check)
npm run doctor                                   # readiness check (create-social-content runs it first)
npm run clean:output -- [--slug <slug>] [--dry-run]   # safe file cleanup: never touches committed files or captions
npm run clean:content -- [--drafts] [--slug <slug>] [--dry-run]   # finished plans; --drafts only after the user agrees; never content/schedule or committed files
npm run clean:merged -- [--apply] [--grace <days>] [--slug <slug>]   # finished (merged + posted) content; --apply only on a cleanup/* branch, via a PR the user agrees to
npm run clean:branches -- [--dry-run]                 # delete local content/tooling/cleanup branches whose PR is merged
npm run typecheck
```
Buffer channel ids: GitHub → Actions → "List Buffer channels" → commit the JSON to `config/buffer-channels.json`.

## Rules

- **Antigravity support is generated, not hand-written.** After you change `CLAUDE.md`, a skill or an agent, run `npm run sync:antigravity` and commit `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/`. CI (`--check`) fails a content PR when they are stale. Skill and agent files need a `name` that matches their folder or file, and a one-line `description`.
- **Skills are the user's only interface; Claude Code AI does everything.** The user types a skill command (or plain words) and never runs `npm` or `git` themselves. Do all terminal, Git and `gh` work yourself, and use `scripts/` as your own tools. Never answer with "run this command". Do it, or say what only the user can do (repo write access, the `BUFFER_API_KEY` secret, Buffer account connections, store contact details). When you add or change a user-facing capability, add or update its skill **and** its use cases in `docs/SKILLS.md`.
- **All posts and reels are made through the skills only.** Start every content request with the matching create skill (`create-social-content` for posts, stories and reels, `create-social-poster`, `create-social-banner`): product photo + product + audience → per-platform deliverables → captions → QA → `monavi-brand-guardian` PASS → `open-content-pr`. Agents never render or edit creatives; fixes go back through the skills. No ad-hoc HTML, image edits or video encodes outside `scripts/render-*.ts`.
- **Quality bar:** never upscale photos and never ship below platform size. The quality gate failing is a blocker. `--allow-lowres`/`--draft` renders are marked `draftOnly` and cannot be published (both the CLI and the CI refuse them).
- **One command → PR, like automation's `/new-blog`.** A `create-social-content` request runs end to end without approval pauses and pushes a `content/<slug>` branch with a PR; that request is the go-ahead. The PR is where the user reviews and edits, and **merging is the approval** that schedules it in Buffer through GitHub Actions. It stops before pushing on a quality-gate failure, a brand-guardian `ESCALATE` or failure after 2 fix rounds, or a missing fact. Any other push or PR still needs the user's confirmation. Never publish directly to Buffer without a dry run and the user's go-ahead.
- Buffer `isAiGenerated` is never sent unless `--ai-disclosure` is passed (or `"aiDisclosure": true` on a plan item).
- **The 5 Golden Editorial Principles (`brand/FASHION_EDITORIAL_PLAYBOOK.md`):**
  1. **Continuous Single-Environment Background:** Harmonize left-right visuals or use full-bleed `overlay` with natural architectural shadow scrims. Never use clashing split backgrounds (e.g. cold slate beside warm sandstone haveli).
  2. **Complete Garment Visibility Mandate:** For multi-piece ethnic wear (kurta pajama, sherwani churidar, lehenga choli), framing must be full-length or 3/4 standing (head to below knees/ankles) showing both top and bottom with footwear on solid ground. Never crop at the waist or thighs.
  3. **Zero-AI Photorealism & Optical Fidelity:** Ban AI buzzwords (`8k, photorealistic, ultra-detailed, masterpiece`). Enforce physical 50mm f/2.8 lens mechanics, natural skin pores, realistic stubble, raw fabric slub, and directional physical ground contact shadows under feet.
  4. **Product Clarity in Headlines:** Headline must prominently name the exact featured product (`Silk Kurta\nPajama.`, `Royal\nSherwani.`) for instant 0.1s comprehension.
  5. **Minimalist Luxury Layout:** Keep image typography minimal with a concise attribute triplet (`Raw Silk | Antique Zari | Tailored Fit`) and at least 400px of clean architectural negative space.
- **Clean, Modern & Photorealistic Human Model Mandate:** When creating fashion campaigns without user-uploaded photos (Workflow A), always generate photorealistic Indian fashion campaign imagery (`npm run fashion:image`) featuring real models wearing the authentic garments with natural skin texture, accurate human anatomy, rich drapery, and commercial editorial lighting. Never use abstract vector silhouettes, 2D icons, or generic placeholders for model photography. When a product photo is supplied (Workflow B), preserve 100% of authentic garment pixels, colors, textures, and embroidery while generating a luxury architectural setting. Keep the `<photo>.ai.json` sidecar for provenance.
- **High-Converting Anti-Slop Branding:** Every creative must follow high-end editorial publication aesthetics directly matching the 8 reference blueprints in `brand/reference-posts/`: prominent vector logo with clear space equal to the star mark, high-contrast Playfair Display headlines, letterspaced Montserrat attribute triplets (` | ` separated), rounded pill CTA buttons, and category badges placed on uncluttered negative space. Never use busy, cluttered, or cheap social media templates.
- No `.env` file. `BUFFER_API_KEY` lives only as a GitHub repository secret. Never write it to any file (the repo is public).
- Never invent prices, offers, addresses or store hours (`brand.json → contact` is the only source).
- TypeScript must stay erasable-only (no `enum`, `namespace` or parameter properties), and imports use `.ts` extensions. Run `npm run typecheck` after edits.

## Using this repo from Antigravity

This file is generated from `CLAUDE.md` for Google Antigravity. The skills are in `.agents/skills/` and the agents in `.agents/agents/`. Everything above applies as written, with this wording mapped:

| The instructions say | In Antigravity |
|---|---|
| "Claude", "Claude Code" | You, the agent in Antigravity |
| `/create-social-content` and the other `/commands` | The same skill names: type `/<skill-name>` in the message box, then the details as normal text. Skills also start on their own when a request matches their description |
| "Read" a file or an image | Open it with your file viewer (for example `view_file`). Always look at every rendered image before saying it is fine |
| "Write" or "Edit" a file | Create or edit the file with your file tools |
| "Run `npm run …`", "`git …`", "`gh …`" | Run it in the terminal (for example `run_command`), and do it yourself. The user never runs these |
| "Run the `monavi-brand-guardian`, `monavi-content-strategist` or `caption-writer` agent" | Invoke that sub-agent from `.agents/agents/`. If sub-agents are not available, read its file and carry out its steps yourself as a separate, careful pass |
| Skills marked "hidden" or "internal" | They show up in the slash menu here. Users only need the ones listed under "user commands" |

The sub-agents here have no tool list, so "review only" and "plans only" are rules of their text: `monavi-brand-guardian` and `monavi-content-strategist` must never edit, render, or open PRs.

Edit `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/`, never this file or `.agents/`. After a change, run `npm run sync:antigravity` and commit the result. CI fails when they are out of date.
